template: Suddly (not shown; the reel is about Aquarii)
version: v9 (lock film: security, new method, no water)
concept: A padlock pops open, attackers stream into the site through the gap; it snaps shut and the site's frame turns into a guard that bounces every attacker off while the checklist ticks. LOCKED. WATCHED. HANDLED. DM us.
motionStyle: vector, poster-first key frames, springs (bold for slams, default for moves), swing curves for the swarm, snap departures
typeTreatment: Archivo black display, red pills, lime checks, slam stack
grade: near black #0d0d12, violet #8b7bff, alarm red #ff4d4d, lime #c6ff3d
sound: effects only: whoosh per camera whip, impact per crack and patch, riser into the dive; Instagram audio: downtempo with a drop at 12.9 s
notes: Why a third cut: cut 2 rebuilt a reference reel (pendulum 'Need X? We got you.' + radial 'Screenshot this'); the owner called it plagiarism, rightly. Now check.mjs allows at most one part per reference reel, never as the payoff, and bans the references' lines (scripts/film/sources.json); this film uses none. Pass 1: leaks were tiny dots at the frame edge -> narrower window, bigger drops, a continuous jet whose thickness follows the water depth. Message chips bunched under the bar -> they rise through the water from mid-height like bubbles, staggered end heights, kept left of Instagram's button column. Patches stayed visible at the loop -> vessel gets loopAt (replays its frame-0 state under the flood). Pass 2-3: send-line accent unreadable (blue on dark pill -> red); service line wrapped (tighter tracking). Fill meter 0 of 25 tight. v2 (owner: 'boring, while it has motion graphics'): the v1 film was one locked-off wide shot with captions. Rebuilt as cinematography: P.camera (keyed, shake, crisp canvas transform), P.vessel films through it, glass shards on each crack, giant slam words instead of captions, P.underwater dive payoff, P.dripWord wet type, P.grain. Passes: grain too heavy (.06 -> .025); patches landed in a small wide shot -> one close-up per patch with a kick; underwater cards bunched low and ran off the side -> faster depth speeds, start before the dive, kept inside the 26 px margins; removed the redundant underwater caption. WhatsApp number removed (owner: DM only). Fill meter 1 of 28 tight. Frame-by-frame pass (owner: 'why not capture frame by frame?'): new scripts/film/frame-review.py over all 540 frames. Found and fixed: 1 s dead hold after the pull-back (re-timed, pains start at 2.9); red words unreadable on water (now solid slabs); bead-like jets (tapered ribbon + velocity-stretched drops with highlights + mist); flat water (depth gradient, light bands, flecks, meniscus); tiny sublines (14 px white); flat aqua frames while riding the pour (wider camera); underwater cards bunched low (bigger, spread, already rising at the dive); motionless 2 s CTA (rippling light, floating type, slow push); handheld drift on every shot. Second review: no frozen stretches; the flagged jumps are the planned whips; loop seamless (5.4). Easing pass (motion focus 14 Oct): every move on the new toolkit (springs/beziers), camera moves summed instead of chained, smooth impulse punch, shake 6-7 Hz from zero, buoyant bubbles, hero reveals (DM us, hook on loop) scale 0.92->1 on the default spring with opacity full by frame 6. --motion-check: no jumps, no linear motion, presets PASS (bold 4.9%/12 frames, default 0%/16, fade 0%/6, swing, snap), grep clean. Hybrid (owner: 'go hybrid, water realism first'): water realism pass on the 3D tank (ripple normals, caustics, meniscus, bubbles, splashes, puddle), then P.tank3d cut into the film for the opening (0-2.35), the refill + dive (11.62-12.88) and the loop return; the 2D vessel hides in those windows. Fixed: the dive camera passed through the glass (muddy) -> it now pushes down onto the surface from above; breath dim softened for 3D. Owner: no water (Aquarii is only a name) and upload today, rendered on GitHub. Re-made as the lock film with the new method; local work limited to a few stills.
